title: How the ‘luteal uglies’ impact women during their periods
description:
Across social media young women are discussing the "luteal uglies." These are changes in appearance and mood that women experience during the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle. We hear from women in Vietnam, the Philippines, and the UK about the symptoms they experience, from acne and bloating to fatigue and brain fog.

But what’s behind these changes? Dr Helen O'Neill, an associate professor in reproductive and molecular genetics at University College London, explains how changing hormone levels impact women’s bodies and their brains. She also offers some tips and coping strategies.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討社群媒體上熱門的「黃體期變醜」 (luteal uglies) 現象，以及女性在月經黃體期所面臨的生理與心理變化。節目邀請倫敦大學學院 (UCL) 副教授 Helen O'Neill 博士拆解背後的科學機制，指出黃體期因雌激素與黃體素急劇下降，導致油脂分泌增加、水腫與痘痘生成，並影響腦部血清素與受體功能，引發情緒低落、焦慮、腦霧與注意力不集中。 O'Neill 博士建議女性透過記錄月經週期、維持適度運動、改善睡眠衛生並避免飲酒來應對，同時也呼籲男性主動了解女性生理週期，給予更多理解與支持。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart explores the social media trend known as the "luteal uglies"—a term describing the physical and emotional changes many women experience during the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle. Featuring personal accounts from women globally and expert insights from Dr. Helen O'Neill of University College London, the episode explains how sudden drops in estrogen and progesterone trigger symptoms like acne, bloating, mood swings, fatigue, and brain fog. Dr. O'Neill offers practical coping advice, such as tracking menstrual cycles, maintaining light exercise, practicing good sleep hygiene, and avoiding alcohol, while encouraging men to educate themselves to better support the women in their lives.
